It feels like Hollyhock is undergoing an identity crisis.   I have been coming for more than 20 years. Over the past 5-7 years HH seems to have lost its focus as sacred retreat space.  During the last two retreats I attended
screaming children were often in the “spa” where the sign asks guests to “whisper or enjoy in silence”
while barking dogs were outside the spa space
tourists were walking talking around taking pictures
loud groups were drinking alcohol on the deck

and families were camping and children screaming well past 10pm in the once quiet and sacred forest camping sites.    I remember HH used to have family programs designed specifically for families.  I think that is a good idea to have separate adult-only and family retreats. As an adult expecting a sacred retreat space
I would like to know that the retreats I am signing up for are adult-only on campus.  The container is what makes retreat and transformation possible and right now

It does not feel like anyone is intentionally creating and holding a retreat-space container at Hollyhock.  I am hopeful that the incoming leader will help repair what has been broken and create new sacred space for transformation.
